chapters.title: The Ascension and a New Witness
chapters.synopsis: Jesus promises the apostles power from the Holy Ghost and charges them to be witnesses in Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, and to the uttermost part of the earth, then ascends into heaven from the mount of Olives as two angels promise his return in like manner. Back in Jerusalem the disciples choose Matthias by lot to replace Judas among the twelve.

segments.speaker: jesus-christ
segments.note: Ye shall be witnesses unto the uttermost part

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: The ascension from the mount of Olives

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Matthias chosen to replace Judas

chapters.title: The Spirit Poured Out at Pentecost
chapters.synopsis: On the day of Pentecost the Holy Ghost falls on the gathered disciples with a sound of rushing wind and tongues of fire, and they speak in tongues understood by devout Jews from every nation. Peter stands and testifies to the multitude that this fulfils Joel's prophecy and that the crucified Jesus is both Lord and Christ, and about three thousand souls are baptized that day.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: The Spirit falls with tongues of fire

segments.speaker: peter
segments.note: This Jesus hath God made both Lord and Christ

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Three thousand baptized; the saints together

chapters.title: Silver and Gold Have I None
chapters.synopsis: At the temple gate called Beautiful, Peter heals a man lame from birth in the name of Jesus Christ, and the man leaps up walking and praising God. As the amazed people gather, Peter testifies that it is faith in Christ's name, not his own power, that has made the man whole, and calls all Israel to repent and be converted.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: A lame man healed at the temple gate

segments.speaker: peter
segments.note: Repent and be converted, that your sins be blotted out

chapters.title: We Cannot but Speak
chapters.synopsis: The priests and Sadducees, troubled at the apostles' preaching of the resurrection, arrest Peter and John, but the rulers can find no way to punish them since the healed man stands before them. Peter and John answer boldly that they cannot but speak the things they have seen and heard, and the released apostles join the believers in prayer, after which the place is shaken and all are filled with the Holy Ghost.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Peter and John arrested and testify before the council

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: The believers pray together and are filled with the Spirit

chapters.title: We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men
chapters.synopsis: Ananias and Sapphira fall dead for lying to the Holy Ghost about the price of their land, and great fear comes upon the church as the apostles work many signs and wonders. The apostles are imprisoned but freed by an angel in the night, and brought again before the council Peter declares that they ought to obey God rather than men, until Gamaliel's counsel spares them from death.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Ananias and Sapphira lie to the Holy Ghost

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Signs and wonders; an angel frees the apostles

segments.speaker: peter
segments.note: We ought to obey God rather than men

chapters.title: A Man Full of Faith
chapters.synopsis: As the number of disciples multiplies, murmuring arises over the neglect of Grecian widows, and the apostles have seven men chosen to serve tables, including Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost. Stephen does great wonders among the people, and when men of the synagogue cannot resist his wisdom, they suborn false witnesses and bring him before the council.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Seven are chosen to serve, including Stephen

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Stephen is falsely accused before the council

chapters.title: Stephen's Witness and Martyrdom
chapters.synopsis: Before the council, Stephen recounts Israel's history from Abraham through Joseph and Moses to Solomon's temple, showing how the fathers always resisted the Holy Ghost and slew the prophets who foretold the Just One. Cut to the heart, the council gnashes on him, but Stephen, full of the Holy Ghost, sees Jesus standing on the right hand of God and is stoned outside the city while Saul consents to his death.

segments.speaker: stephen
segments.note: Stephen recounts Israel's history and its rebellion

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Stephen is stoned and forgives his killers

chapters.title: Philip and the Ethiopian
chapters.synopsis: Persecution scatters the saints from Jerusalem, and Philip goes down to Samaria preaching Christ, where many believe and are baptized, including Simon the sorcerer, who is rebuked for trying to buy the gift of God with money. An angel then sends Philip to a desert road, where he teaches an Ethiopian official from Isaiah's prophecy and baptizes him.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Philip preaches in Samaria; Simon rebuked

segments.speaker: philip-evangelist
segments.note: The Ethiopian is taught from Isaiah and baptized

chapters.title: Saul Is Turned on the Damascus Road
chapters.synopsis: Breathing threats against the disciples, Saul is struck down by a light from heaven on the road to Damascus and hears the Lord's voice asking why he persecutes him. Blind for three days, he is healed and baptized, and immediately begins to preach Christ in the synagogues, to the astonishment of all who knew him as a persecutor. Peter, traveling among the saints, heals Aeneas and raises Dorcas from the dead at Joppa.

segments.note: Saul is converted on the road to Damascus

segments.note: Saul preaches Christ in the synagogues

segments.speaker: luke

chapters.title: God Is No Respecter of Persons
chapters.synopsis: Cornelius, a devout Roman centurion, is told in a vision to send for Peter, while Peter himself is prepared by a vision of a sheet of unclean animals to learn that he should call no man common or unclean. Peter goes to Cornelius's house and testifies that God is no respecter of persons, and while he yet speaks, the Holy Ghost falls on the Gentiles, who are baptized.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Cornelius is told in a vision to send for Peter

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Peter's vision of the sheet from heaven

segments.speaker: peter
segments.note: God is no respecter of persons

chapters.title: Then Hath God Granted Repentance
chapters.synopsis: Peter returns to Jerusalem and defends his preaching to Gentiles by recounting his vision and the Spirit's outpouring on Cornelius's household, and the brethren conclude that God has granted repentance unto life to the Gentiles also. The gospel spreads to Antioch, where Barnabas is sent to strengthen the growing church and the disciples are first called Christians.

segments.note: Peter defends preaching the gospel to Gentiles

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: The church at Antioch; disciples first called Christians

chapters.title: Peter Is Freed by an Angel
chapters.synopsis: Herod kills James the brother of John and imprisons Peter, intending to bring him out to the people after the passover, but an angel of the Lord leads Peter past the sleeping guards and the iron gate to freedom while the church prays for him. Herod, struck by an angel for accepting worship as a god, is eaten of worms and dies, while the word of God grows and multiplies.

segments.note: An angel leads Peter out of prison

chapters.title: Sent Forth from Antioch
chapters.synopsis: The Holy Ghost calls Barnabas and Saul to their missionary work, and the church at Antioch sends them forth with fasting and prayer. On Cyprus they strike the sorcerer Elymas blind before the deputy, and at Antioch in Pisidia Paul preaches in the synagogue that through Christ is preached the forgiveness of sins, so that many Gentiles believe though the Jews are stirred to persecution.

chapters.title: We Also Are Men of Like Passions
chapters.synopsis: At Iconium Paul and Barnabas preach boldly despite a plot to stone them, and at Lystra, after healing a man crippled from birth, they must restrain the crowds who would worship them as gods, protesting that they too are only men. Paul is stoned and left for dead at Lystra but rises and continues on, and the missionaries return through the cities strengthening the new disciples.

segments.note: Paul and Barnabas preach at Iconium

chapters.title: The Council at Jerusalem
chapters.synopsis: A dispute arises over whether Gentile converts must be circumcised after the law of Moses, and the apostles and elders gather at Jerusalem, where Peter, Paul, and Barnabas testify of God's work among the Gentiles and James proposes that they be spared this burden. Letters are sent confirming the decision, but Paul and Barnabas afterward part ways over whether to take John Mark on their next journey.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: The council debates the law of Moses for Gentiles

segments.speaker: luke

chapters.title: Come Over into Macedonia
chapters.synopsis: Paul takes on Timothy at Lystra, and in a night vision a man of Macedonia begs him to come and help them, so the company sails for Philippi. There Lydia, a seller of purple, believes and is baptized with her household, and after Paul casts a spirit of divination out of a servant girl, he and Silas are beaten and imprisoned, only to be freed by an earthquake and to baptize their jailer's whole household.

chapters.title: The Unknown God at Mars Hill
chapters.synopsis: Paul reasons in the synagogues at Thessalonica and Berea, where many search the scriptures daily to see whether these things are so, though persecution follows him from city to city. At Athens, provoked by a city full of idols, Paul stands on Mars Hill and preaches that the God who made the world, whom they ignorantly worship as an unknown god, has appointed a day of judgment through the man he raised from the dead.

segments.note: Paul preaches at Thessalonica and Berea

chapters.title: I Have Much People in This City
chapters.synopsis: At Corinth Paul labors with Aquila and Priscilla, tentmakers, and is told in a vision that the Lord has much people in that city, so he continues preaching there for a year and a half despite being brought before Gallio. He then sails for Syria, leaving Aquila and Priscilla at Ephesus, where Apollos, an eloquent believer, is taught the way of God more perfectly.

segments.note: Paul labors at Corinth; brought before Gallio

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Apollos taught more perfectly at Ephesus

chapters.title: Mightily Grew the Word of God at Ephesus
chapters.synopsis: At Ephesus Paul finds disciples who had not heard of the Holy Ghost, and after he baptizes and lays hands on them they receive the gift and prophesy. Paul's mighty works expose the seven sons of Sceva who try vainly to cast out devils in Jesus's name without belief, and the word of God grows mightily, until Demetrius the silversmith stirs a great riot over the loss of trade in idols of Diana.

chapters.title: None of These Things Move Me
chapters.synopsis: At Troas Paul raises Eutychus, a young man who had fallen dead from a window during his long preaching, then sails toward Jerusalem. Calling the elders of Ephesus to Miletus, he testifies that he has kept back nothing profitable, declares that none of these things move him, neither counts he his life dear, and warns them to watch for grievous wolves, before they part in tears.

chapters.title: Bound in Spirit to Jerusalem
chapters.synopsis: Warned by prophecy at Tyre and by Agabus at Caesarea that bonds and afflictions await him, Paul insists he is ready not only to be bound but to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus. Arriving at Jerusalem, he is seized in the temple by a mob that would kill him, until the chief captain rescues him and permits Paul to speak to the people.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Warnings of bonds; Paul is ready to die at Jerusalem

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Paul seized in the temple and rescued by the captain

chapters.title: Paul's Defense to the Multitude
chapters.synopsis: Standing on the stairs before the hostile crowd, Paul recounts in Hebrew his own conversion on the road to Damascus and his call to bear Christ's name to the Gentiles. When the mention of the Gentiles enrages the multitude to cry for his death, the chief captain orders him scourged, but Paul stays the lash by declaring his birthright as a Roman citizen.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Paul recounts his conversion and call to the Gentiles

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Paul claims his rights as a Roman citizen

chapters.title: As Thou Hast Testified in Jerusalem
chapters.synopsis: Before the council Paul divides the Pharisees and Sadducees by declaring his hope in the resurrection, and that night the Lord stands by him, promising that as he has testified in Jerusalem he must also bear witness at Rome. When forty men vow to kill Paul, his nephew reveals the plot, and the chief captain sends him under heavy guard to Felix the governor at Caesarea.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Before the council; the Lord promises Rome

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: A plot uncovered; Paul sent to Felix

chapters.title: Almost Thou Persuadest Me
chapters.synopsis: Accused by the high priest's orator Tertullus of being a pestilent troublemaker, Paul answers Felix that he worships the God of his fathers and lives in hope of the resurrection of the just and unjust. Felix, trembling as Paul reasons of righteousness and judgment to come, delays decision and leaves Paul bound for two years, hoping for a bribe.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Tertullus accuses Paul before Felix

segments.note: Paul's hope in the resurrection of the dead

chapters.title: I Appeal unto Caesar
chapters.synopsis: Festus succeeds Felix and, under pressure from the Jews, asks Paul if he will go up to Jerusalem to be judged, but Paul, discerning the danger, appeals to Caesar as a Roman citizen. When King Agrippa and Bernice come to Caesarea, Festus lays Paul's case before them, uncertain what charge to send with him to Rome.

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Paul appeals unto Caesar before Festus

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Festus presents Paul's case to Agrippa

chapters.title: Almost Thou Persuadest Me to Be a Christian
chapters.synopsis: Before King Agrippa, Paul recounts his zealous life as a Pharisee, his vision of the risen Lord on the Damascus road, and his commission to open the eyes of Jews and Gentiles alike and turn them from darkness to light. Agrippa answers that Paul almost persuades him to be a Christian, and the king and Festus agree that Paul might have been set free had he not appealed to Caesar.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.note: Paul's vision and commission on the Damascus road

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian

chapters.title: The Storm and the Shipwreck
chapters.synopsis: Sailing for Rome as a prisoner, Paul warns the ship's company against setting out, and when a tempestuous wind called Euroclydon drives them for many days without sight of sun or stars, all hope of being saved is taken away. An angel assures Paul that though the ship will be lost, not a life will perish, and the vessel finally breaks apart on a shoal, yet all two hundred and seventy-six aboard come safely to land.

segments.note: The voyage begins; the great storm rises

segments.speaker: luke
segments.note: An angel's promise; all come safe to land

chapters.title: Preaching at Rome Unhindered
chapters.synopsis: Shipwrecked on Malta, Paul shakes off a viper unharmed and heals the father of the island's chief man, so that the people take him for a god. Arriving at last in Rome, Paul calls the local Jewish leaders together to explain his case, and though many disbelieve his testimony of Christ from the law and the prophets, he dwells two years in his own hired house, preaching the kingdom of God unhindered.
